strain: C57BL/6J (wild type and 5-HT2A-/- backcrossed onto C57BL/6J)

age.evidence: All the experiments were conducted with animals aged from postnatal day 60.

sex.evidence: Wild-type male and female C57BL/6J mice were purchased from Charles River Laboratories... Mice from both sexes were indifferently used in behavioral experiments.

dosing.evidence: 2,5-Dimethoxy-4-iodoamphetamine (DOI; Sigma D101)... were injected intraperitoneally at the dose of 1 mg/kg... For microdosing experiments, DOI and psilocybin were injected daily at the dose of 0.05 mg/kg... during 6 days. DOI... dissolved in saline solution (0.9% NaCl).

psilocybin (Cayman Chemical No.14041)... were injected intraperitoneally at the dose of 1 mg/kg... Psilocybin and Lisuride were first dissolved in DMSO and then diluted in saline solution (DMSO 1.5%, 0.9% NaCl). For microdosing experiments... 0.05 mg/kg... during 6 days.
Lisuride maleate (Santa Cruz Biotechnologies) were injected intraperitoneally at the dose of 1 mg/kg... first dissolved in DMSO and then diluted in saline solution (DMSO 1.5%, 0.9% NaCl).

assays.assay_description: HTRs counted by a blind observer over 30 min after i.p. vehicle, DOI (1 or 0.05 mg/kg), psilocybin (1 or 0.05 mg/kg) or lisuride (1 mg/kg) in WT and 5-HT2A-/- mice; data binned in 10-min frames. Apparatus not described.

application_type.evidence: DOI (1 mg/kg, i.p.) or psilocybin (1 mg/kg, i.p.) or lisuride (1 mg/kg, i.p.) or DOI (0.05 mg/kg, i.p.) or psilocybin (0.05 mg/kg, i.p.)

setup_restrain.evidence: HTR counted as a head flick by observer; no restraint mentioned

food_restriction.evidence: No food described in the observation setting

water_restriction.evidence: No water described in the observation setting

time_to_assay.evidence: HTRs were monitored over 30 min after the administration

outcomes.summary: DOI and psilocybin (1 mg/kg) significantly increased HTRs in WT mice across all three 10-min bins, whereas lisuride had no effect. DOI and psilocybin did not induce HTR in 5-HT2A-/- mice, and microdoses (0.05 mg/kg) did not significantly increase HTR.
outcomes.evidence: administration of DOI or psilocybin induced a significant increase in HTR in wild type mice, compared to vehicle-injected animals... whereas administration of lisuride had no effect

B1_num_measures.evidence: HTR was counted as a head flick by a blind observer (time bins are the same measure).

B7_automated_classification.evidence: HTR was counted as a head flick by a blind observer.

D1_continuity.evidence: HTRs were monitored over 30 min after the administration

assays.assay_description: After 24 h food deprivation, mice placed in a 50-cm square open field with ~2 cm wooden bedding under 1000 lux, food pellet in centre; latency to bite measured (10 min max), followed by 5-min food consumption in a test cage. Run in WT and 5-HT2A-/- CDM mice after single 1 mg/kg DOI/psilocybin/lisuride (± WAY-100635, SCH23390, eticlopride) or 6-day microdosing.

application_type.evidence: mice were injected either with vehicle, or DOI (1 mg/kg, i.p.), or psilocybin (1 mg/kg, i.p.)... or lisuride (1 mg/kg, i.p.) (antagonists SCH23390/eticlopride given s.c.)

setup_restrain.evidence: Each mouse was placed in the same corner of the open field

food_restriction.evidence: Twenty-four hours prior to behavioral testing, the food was removed from the home cage.

water_restriction.evidence: No water described in the open field during the test

time_to_assay.evidence: Mice received an injection... They were then subjected to tests... from 2 to 15 days after the injection; The first behavioral test was performed 48 h after the last injection of psychedelics.

outcomes.summary: Single-dose DOI, psilocybin and lisuride decreased latency to feed in WT CDM mice. DOI and lisuride effects were absent in 5-HT2A-/- CDM mice, whereas psilocybin remained effective (also with WAY-100635). Psilocybin microdosing reduced latency; DOI microdosing only tended to. 1 mg/kg psilocybin increased post-test food intake, which microdosing did not.
outcomes.statistics: Fig1B Kruskal-Wallis H=18.16; CDM vs naive p=0.005; DOI p=0.015; psilocybin p=0.002; lisuride p=0.003. Fig2A H=35.19; DOI p>0.999; lisuride p>0.999. Fig3A H=33.36; psilocybin p<0.001; WAY+psilocybin p=0.005. Fig4A Welch ANOVA 10.98 (3.000, 15.40); mDOI p=0.152; mPsilocybin p<0.001. S5C food intake psilocybin p=0.029.
outcomes.evidence: Administration of either DOI or psilocybin to CDM mice induced a significant decrease in the latency to feed in the NSF test... Similar results were obtained in lisuride-injected CDM mice

B1_num_measures.evidence: The latency to eat... was measured... The amount of pellet eaten for 5 min was measured.

B4_ethological.evidence: Latency to bite pellet and food amount; no distinct natural behaviours scored

assays.assay_description: 48 h two-bottle habituation in home cage, 12 h adaptation in testing cage, 24 h food/water deprivation, then 12 h two-bottle choice (1% sucrose vs water); bottles weighed; preference index computed. WT and 5-HT2A-/- CDM mice, single-dose and microdosing regimens, with antagonist pretreatments.

application_type.evidence: DOI (1 mg/kg, i.p.), or psilocybin (1 mg/kg, i.p.)... or lisuride (1 mg/kg, i.p.)

setup_habituation.evidence: They were then transferred to the testing cage for 12 h with food and water ad libitum for adaptation.

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice freely access bottles in cage

food_restriction.evidence: Thereafter, they were deprived of both food and water for 24 h.

water_restriction.evidence: Thereafter, they were deprived of both food and water for 24 h.

time_to_assay.evidence: tests were performed from 2 to 15 days after a single intraperitoneal injection (exact SPT day not stated; follows NSF)

outcomes.summary: Single-dose DOI, psilocybin and lisuride restored sucrose preference in WT CDM mice to naive levels. DOI and lisuride were ineffective in 5-HT2A-/- CDM mice, whereas psilocybin (± WAY-100635) remained effective. Microdosing DOI or psilocybin also increased sucrose preference.
outcomes.statistics: Fig1C F(4,83)=5.473; CDM vs naive p<0.001; DOI p=0.002; psilocybin p=0.010; lisuride p=0.010. Fig2B H=11.74; DOI p=0.182; lisuride p>0.999. Fig3B H=23.41; psilocybin p<0.001; WAY+psilocybin p<0.001. Fig4B F(3,30)=8.189; mDOI p=0.006; mPsilocybin p=0.008.
outcomes.evidence: DOI and psilocybin administration to CDM mice also restored sucrose preference to a level similar to that measured in non-conditioned mice

outcomes.summary: Single-dose DOI, psilocybin and lisuride decreased immobility in WT CDM mice. DOI and lisuride were ineffective in 5-HT2A-/- CDM mice, whereas psilocybin remained effective even with WAY-100635, SCH23390 or eticlopride pretreatment. Microdosing DOI or psilocybin also decreased immobility.

judge_notes: All three candidates identified the same five assays (HTR, NSF, SPT, FST, cyclotron); merged WT, 5-HT2A-/-, antagonist, and microdosing variants into single assays per rubric.
NSF 5-min post-test food consumption kept within the NSF assay as its second measure (B1 = 2-3).
HTR B1 set to 0 (single measure): 10-min bins are temporal dynamics (B2), not separate measures — overrode modal score 1.
FST B1 set to 0: only immobility is reported; overrode deepseek/gemma score 1.
SPT D2 set to 3 (>6 h; 12 h test) per qwen and deepseek's evidence; gemma's score 2 contradicted its own 12 h evidence.

SPT E3 bedding set to 0/low: bedding in the testing cage is not stated, so inference was rejected. SPT E1 kept as Home cage (medium): the test occurs in a 'testing cage' after 12 h adaptation, not the original home cage.
SPT B1 set to 2-3: the paper reports total volume intake alongside the preference index.
NSF E8 kept 0 (modal): the single pellet is the test stimulus and no water is available. D5 = Yes for NSF, SPT and FST, since all were tested 2-15 days post-injection (overrode gemma).
Time_to_assay for SPT and FST: exact days are not stated beyond the 2-15 day window, so value_minutes is null with low confidence.
n_total left null for NSF, SPT and FST because cohorts and shared control groups span multiple figures. n_per_group_min = 7, from the microdosing cohort (Fig 4).

Dosing schedule for DOI and psilocybin recorded as acute (modal); the 6-day 0.05 mg/kg microdosing arm is noted in evidence. Psilocybin and lisuride vehicle recorded as DMSO, the first-listed solvent (diluted in saline).

sex_dependent set to not_reported: both sexes were used but sex was not analysed as a factor. dose_dependent set to not_reported for the antidepressant assays: single-dose and microdose regimens were not statistically compared.
